reasons.B: Wine-and-gold feast queen: a wine bell skirt flaring from the hip, a gold butterfly bodice and a candle crown, the richest and most epic read from the high camera and apart from every other family (second critic 6.85, first; first critic 6.08, second).
reasons.A: Ivory court gown: the most elegant bodice, gold with a chain necklace, over a true A-line skirt under a veil of candle spikes; the prettiest dress of the run (5.98, second; first critic 5.35, third).
reasons.F: Sun-disc queen: the run's best invention, a sun-disc crown and ruff collar over a pleated gold skirt that flares at the front, the only one that reads as gold from far off (5.70, third; first critic 6.53, first).

fixes.B: The full-width wine sleeves make the top a broad slab: slim them with gold cuffs, round the hem, and let shade-black creep up the front.
fixes.A: Too pale for the night and drifting toward linen: make the skirt wine or deep gold over ivory, slim the banded sleeves, and add shade-black at the hem.
fixes.F: All one saturated gold reads as a gold box from above: make the bodice and sleeves wine or dark gold, keep bright gold for trim, and carry the flare and stripes round the back.

notes: EPIC set. 6 of 6 survived the draft and the rework with no resume (g00 and g02 hit the 40-turn rework cap with their sets passing). Each set put Neon on about three small parts as asked (D on six), but from the camera the glow and the shade-black souring barely show in any. Shoulder-wide block sleeves on all six again: the brief's slim-sleeve ask did not land. The best mix: B's skirt and bodice, F's crown and ruff, A's necklace.
